newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices close flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices close flat to lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Monday's lightly traded session anywhere from flat to down 1/2 point overall, while on the short end one trader cited a curious lack of re-investment cash.

"We expected some money to come running in and re-invest, and it hasn't shown up," the trader said. "And I think that's because the customer base, which is institutional, perceives that it's going to get weaker in the front end."
According to MuniView/Muller Data Corp., U.S. municipal bond redemptions are expected to total $23 billion in January.
That figure includes current and advance refundings, maturing bonds and notes, as well as coupon payments.
As for the long end, the trader judged the muni cash down 1/4 to 1/2 point overall.
Monday's active issues included Florida Board of Education 5-1/2 percent bonds of June 2026. The bonds had a 5.74 percent net bid, versus a 5.72 percent net bid on Friday.
A municipal analyst said broader market prices were unchanged to down 1/4 point overall. Levels were difficult to gauge, however, given thin trade, the analyst said.
High-grade issues closed even to slightly lower, while dollar bonds were down 1/4 point, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 12/32 at 115-5/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 9/32 at 111-9/32. The MOB spread was 124 ticks.
In the government market, the 30-year Treasury bond closed down 1/2 at 96-16/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
In new issues, Tuesday's scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.07 billion in 23 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Competitive sales are seen totaling $457 million in 18 issues. The largest is a two-part $245.8 million Washington general obligation deal at 1130 EST. An analyst, however, said Delaware's $80 million offering will be the deal to watch. Delaware "is in pretty good financial shape," has a "solid double-A" rating and is a relatively infrequent issuer, he said.
"It's probably the most important issue that you are looking at as far as the competitive bond issues."
Standard & Poor's Corp has assigned a AA-plus rating to both the state's existing GOs and Tuesday's new issue.
Negotiated sales total $620 million in five offerings. The largest is a $345.7 million Houston refunding deal through senior manager PaineWebber Inc.
An additional $814 million of deals are on the possible negotiated calendar, meaning underwriters have said they may priced the deals Tuesday depending on market conditions.
